units.text: INT. DRIVE-IN CLIMBING WALL - NIGHT
The back of a derelict drive-in screen, twelve stories of cracked white plywood, now bolted with colored holds and lit by a single sodium lamp.
Weeds push through the empty parking lot below.
A thermos steams on a folding table at the base.
PERPETUA "PEP" ILUNGA, 24, wiry, chalk to the elbows, hangs from a sloping overhang thirty feet up.
Her forearms are knotted.
She breathes through her teeth, reaching for a hold the size of a bottle cap and missing it by an inch.
She swings out, catches herself, and swears softly to the dark.
Her fingers slide off.
She falls, and the rope catches her with a soft whump.
She hangs spinning in her harness, the lot turning below her, then reaches out and grabs the wall again.
She lets out a laugh that is half sob, half triumph.
Again.
units.name: PEP

units.text: She climbs.
Hand over hand, foot to foot, the slow rhythm of someone who has done this route two hundred times.
She reaches the overhang and sticks the bottle cap this time.
Her whole body locks.
She hangs there, shaking, victorious, and for a breath she is perfectly still.
Then a car engine on gravel.
Headlights sweep the wall and pin her, a bug on a screen.
She twists her head.
The car, a dented sedan, idles at the edge of the lot.
A door opens.
BARNABY CROSS, 50s, thin, in a windbreaker and a ball cap, steps out holding a clipboard.
He does not look up.
He walks to the folding table, picks up the thermos, sniffs it, and sets it down.
Perpetua Ilunga?
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: Who's asking?
units.name: PEP

units.text: County. Code enforcement.
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: The word lands like a stone in a pond.
Her grip loosens.
She slips a foot, catches it, and clings on with new fury.
It's private property.
units.name: PEP

units.text: It's a structure over fifty feet without a permit.
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: It's a screen. It's been here since 1962.
units.name: PEP

units.text: That's the problem.
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: She presses her forehead against the plywood.
Below, Barnaby writes something on the clipboard.
Then, to her astonishment, he sets it on the table, takes off his ball cap, and rolls his shoulders.
Is that a V6?
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: What?
units.name: PEP

units.text: The problem you're on. The one with the sloper.
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: Yes?
units.name: PEP

units.text: Left heel hook. Then you can pull through. You're fighting your own hips.
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: She stares at him.
Silence.
Then she shifts her left foot, hooks the heel on a hold, and her hips swing into the wall.
The next move unlocks.
She reaches the top, slaps the lip, and shouts.
It worked!
units.name: PEP

units.text: Barnaby nods.
He picks up the clipboard, tears off a yellow slip, and tucks it under the thermos.
You have thirty days.
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: To do what?
units.name: PEP

units.text: Come see me. I've got a form.
units.name: BARNABY

units.text: She laughs, breathless, and lets go, falling the last of the way down the rope.
Barnaby puts his cap back on, climbs into his car, and drives off.
Pep dangles in the lamp light, turning, the yellow slip fluttering under the thermos.
